baa_10y_spread.proxy_note: Moody's Baa corporate bond yield minus the 10Y Treasury -- a long-run investment-grade credit-risk-premium PROXY, not the literal ICE BofA IG OAS series this system quotes daily. Real history back to 1986. Useful for direction and episode timing (did credit broadly tighten/widen, and when); its magnitude runs tighter than IG OAS and far tighter than HY OAS, so never quote its level as if it were either.

history_digest.sentence: The 10-year TIPS real yield (2.79%, dated 11-24) first reached this level on Sep 24 and has been there on 23 of the 42 sessions since; before this run, the last time was Nov 2008 (during the 2007-09 Global Financial Crisis). This run's high was 2.95% on Oct 5, last matched in Nov 2008. Today's reading is at or above the reading on 99.2 of every 100 days since 2003. But TIPS only exist since 2003: the Cleveland Fed's model real rate, back to 1982, puts real rates at the 81st percentile of the last 30 years and the 54th since 1982 — high against the last 30 years, about average since 1982.
